notes: Brackets: the booklet prints no bracket schedule. It prints a tax table in 50-dollar rows below 7,000 and 100-dollar rows from 7,000 to 100,000 (packet PDF pp.48-51), one table for every filing status, and for 100,000 or more 'Multiply the amount on line 5 by 6%; Subtract $642' ('Use this Tax Rate Schedule for any filing status claimed on the SC1040', packet PDF p.51). Packet PDF p.5: 'the top marginal Individual Income Tax rate changed to 6%'.

Derived schedule (brackets.derivation): 0% from 0, 3% from 3,560, 6% from 17,840, the same for every filing status. Method: every one of the 1,069 printed table rows (50 to 99,900) is reproduced exactly, after rounding to the dollar, by the tax at the row's midpoint; the formula's constant 642 equals 0.03 x (3,560 + 17,840), so the schedule also gives 6% of income minus 642 exactly at 100,000 and above. The table alone fixes the lower threshold only to 3,559-3,566 and the upper to 17,818-17,857; taking the printed 642 as exact fixes their sum at 21,400, and 3,560 / 17,840 is the pair in that set on round tens. Any pair in the set gives the same table to the dollar. 3,560, 17,840 and the 3% rate are not printed in the booklet.

Derivation table rows are recorded with status 'all' because the booklet prints one table for every filing status (the validator checks each row against both the single and married_joint schedules). Their incomes are row midpoints, which the booklet does not print (the row's 'At least' and 'But less than' are printed).

Base: South Carolina starts from federal taxable income (SC1040 line 1, Instructions PDF p.5); a federal taxable income below zero is entered as zero and the negative amount is subtracted on line r. The booklet prints no South Carolina standard deduction and no personal exemption. Printed deductions: the dependent exemption of 4,930 for each dependent (line w) and 4,930 for each dependent under age 6 (line t), claimed in addition to line w.

The age 65 and older deduction (15,000 against any South Carolina income) is recorded as a relief (covers all_income), not a base deduction, because the booklet reduces it by the retirement and military retirement deductions.

How the retirement and age 65 deductions combine (Instructions PDF pp.12-13, worksheets for lines q-1 and q-2 and Examples 1-5): the age 65 deduction is 15,000 less the person's own retirement deduction (p-1 or p-2) and own military retirement deduction (p-4 or p-5), not below zero, so for a person 65 or older the own retirement deduction plus the age 65 deduction cannot exceed 15,000 (Example 2: 10,000 on p-1 and 5,000 on q-1; Example 3: 'The maximum allowed deduction for 2025 is $15,000'). The military retirement deduction is not capped and may exceed 15,000, leaving no age 65 amount (Example 4: 36,000 on p-4 and nothing on q-1). Surviving spouse deductions (p-3, p-6) do not reduce the age 65 deduction.

Retirement deduction 'under age 65' is written as max_age 64 (the oldest age reached that is still under 65) plus the booklet's words in other_conditions; the 65-or-older branch is 'age 65 or older during the tax year', min_age 65.

Surviving spouse retirement deduction (line p-3): the 3,000 or 10,000 limit turns on the age the deceased spouse would have reached had they lived, not the survivor's age, so no min_age or max_age is set on those entries; the age test is in other_conditions.

Qualified retirement income is 'income from plans defined in IRC 401, 403, 408, and 457, and all public employee retirement plans of the federal, state, and local governments, including individual retirement plans, Keogh plans, and military retirement' (Instructions PDF p.11). Because 'all' public employee plans of state governments are named, without limiting them to South Carolina, public_pension_other_state is in covers. Military retirement is in the definition, so military_pension is in covers of the retirement deduction entries; the full military deduction (p-4/p-5) reduces the own-plan cap.
Roth conversions: the booklet does not say whether a conversion is qualified retirement income; roth_conversion is in covers_unclear on the retirement deduction entries.

Social Security: line o subtracts Social Security (Title 2 of the Social Security Act) and railroad retirement taxed on the federal return (Instructions PDF p.10; SC1040 line o, packet PDF p.46), and PDF p.11 says Social Security and railroad retirement income 'are not taxed by South Carolina'. Treatment exempt.

Municipal interest: line d adds back federally exempt interest from obligations of states and political subdivisions other than South Carolina (Instructions PDF p.6); nothing is added back for South Carolina obligations. The booklet does not say in words that South Carolina's own bonds are exempt; the treatment is inferred from the add-back being limited to other states.
Capital gains: line i deducts 44% of net capital gain (net long-term capital gain over net short-term capital loss), long-term holding period as federal (Instructions PDF p.8). No separate rate.

Two Wage Earner Credit (line 12): .007 of the lesser of 50,000 or the lower-earning spouse's South Carolina qualified earned income, at most 350, married filing jointly only (Instructions PDF pp.17-18). Recorded with cap under married_joint only because no other filing status may claim it.

Indexing: the booklet says nothing about inflation adjustment of any figure; the 2025 dependent exemption is described only as an 'Increase In South Carolina Dependent Exemption' to 4,930 (packet PDF p.5). All entries not_stated.

Recapture and surtaxes: none found in the booklet (empty lists mean none found, not that the booklet says there are none). The 6%-minus-642 formula is the ordinary schedule written as one line, not a recapture.

Printed but not recorded as reliefs (out of scope: not retirement or Social Security relief, or a credit other than those): volunteer deduction 6,000 per qualifying volunteer (line j); subsistence allowance 16 per workday for law enforcement, firefighters and EMS (line s); SC College Investment Program and Tuition Prepayment contributions (line k); consumer protection services up to 300 / 1,000 (line u); special needs adoption 2,000 per year per child, Palmetto ABLE, Catastrophe Savings Account and preceptor items (line v); Child and Dependent Care Credit 7% of the federal expense, at most 210 for one child or 420 for two or more (line 11); state tax refund (line f); out-of-state income and losses (lines b, h); state tax addback for itemizers (line a); active trade or business income at a flat 3% by election (line l, line 8, I-335); 2.5% extra tax on excess Catastrophe Savings Account withdrawals (line 9); lump-sum distribution tax (line 7, SC4972).
